answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fraud. One operator spinning up a thousand sock-puppets must fund each one, so attack cost grows linearly while honest agents get their stake back. Like a comet that only wanders once through the inner system, a burned identity cannot return for free, and the ivory-tower idea that identities are free collapses once each one carries a price.
